blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Under a risk floor of 70, two plans tie at the best NPV: P scores (NPV 500, risk 80) and Q scores (NPV 500, risk 95). No plan above the floor has more NPV. Plain ε-constraint, maximizing NPV, returns P. What is P?

options.text: Weakly efficient but not Pareto-optimal, since Q ties its NPV and removes more risk
options.says: Right: no plan beats P strictly on both, but Q dominates it: equal NPV, more risk removed.

options.text: Pareto-optimal, since no plan above the floor has more NPV than P has
options.says: Pareto-optimal needs no plan at least as good on both and better on one; Q is such a plan.

options.text: Not even weakly efficient, since Q is strictly better than P on both objectives
options.says: Q ties P on NPV, so it is not strictly better on both; P is weakly efficient.

options.text: Pareto-optimal, since an answer of an ε problem is always Pareto-optimal
options.says: An ε answer is always at least weakly efficient, and Pareto-optimal only when it is the single optimal plan.

origin.section: Plain ε-Constraint Can Return a Weakly Efficient Plan

questions.stem: An analyst writes AUGMECON's objective as NPV + 1 × s, with NPV in $k and s the risk above the floor in $k, instead of NPV + (0.001 / range) × s. What changes?

options.text: Nothing, since the slack term only ever breaks ties between plans of equal NPV
options.says: With a weight of 1 the slack term can outweigh NPV differences; the lesson's run gave up $945k of NPV.

options.text: The solve fails, since a floor written as an equality makes the model infeasible
options.says: The equality with s at least 0 says the same as the old floor; the model solves.

options.text: The answer can give up NPV for risk above the floor, since the slack acts as a second objective
options.says: Right: it becomes a weighted sum above the floor, no longer the most NPV at that floor.

options.text: The answer always lands exactly on the floor, since the slack now has a cost
options.says: A positive weight rewards slack, it does not charge for it; the run's slack grew to 2,554.

origin.section: Reward the Floor's Slack With a Weight Too Small to Cost Any of the Objective

questions.stem: A sweep steps a whole-number floor by 1. At floor 200 the augmented solve returns a plan whose floored objective is 206, a slack of 6. Which floor should the sweep ask next?

options.text: 201, since every floor of the grid must be solved to be sure of every plan
options.says: Floors 201 to 206 return the same plan; asking them wastes solves.

options.text: 207, since every floor from 200 up to 206 returns this same plan
options.says: Right: the jump is 1 + floor(6 / 1) = 7 floors, the bypass of AUGMECON2.

options.text: 206, since the plan's own value is the next floor to ask about
options.says: At floor 206 the plan still clears the floor, so the solve returns it again.

options.text: 212, since the jump is always twice the slack of the last plan
options.says: The jump is one more than the slack in steps; 212 can skip plans between 207 and 211.

origin.section: Jump Past Floors the Slack Already Covers, and Stop at the First Infeasible One

concepts: which floor a sweep asks after a solve
what the size of the slack weight decides
